text:
Artyom Levshunov was the second overall pick in 2024, taken right after Macklin Celebrini, and his second full season is a grind. He has three points in 20 games and none in his last twelve, playing almost 21 minutes a night on a Chicago team that spends a lot of time defending.

Some of it is luck. The Blackhawks have scored 4.6 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him points. Some of it isn't. Chicago takes only 38% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with Levshunov on, about 4 points worse than without him, and Scott Powers of The Athletic noted that two of Winnipeg's best odd-man rushes on Saturday came from him being too aggressive in the neutral zone. That's a young defenseman learning when to step up.

Context matters: Evolving-Hockey had him playing with some of the weakest teammates in the league last season. History also says patience: 16 of the 17 defensemen picked first to fourth since 2005 with four-plus seasons reached 200 games, with a median first full season of 0.36 points a game. He's at 0.15 this year. Our talent range has him around 23 points.
